modes.name: Flow tracers
modes.author: moran
modes.description: NASA's real-time precipitation (IMERG) over the continents, with streams of particles following the rain's motion. Yellow tracers over rain sing: heavier rain plays higher and louder, west to east pans left to right.

modes.name: Layered maps
modes.summary: One gas at a time, from NASA's GEOS-CF model. Higher values play higher notes in that gas's own instrument; hover, touch or use the arrow keys.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Pick one gas with the Dataset menu (ozone, carbon monoxide or nitrogen oxides): the map shows that gas and you hear only it, in its own instrument and pitch range (carbon monoxide low, ozone in the middle, nitrogen oxides higher). Higher values play higher notes. Hover, touch or use the arrow keys.

modes.name: Mapping lab
modes.summary: Hundreds of points across the map play a note when the gas rises past a threshold. Choose what drives pitch, loudness and pan under More.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: About 300 grid points play a note when the data rises past a threshold. Choose what drives each part of the sound (pitch, loudness, pan, brightness, depth, attack, timbre family) from longitude, latitude, value or change, flip any mapping, try presets, and share the mapping by link. Hover or use the arrow keys to hear one point and hear how it was mapped.

modes.name: Ozone probe
modes.summary: Near-surface ozone from NASA's GEOS-CF model. Hover, touch or use the arrow keys: more ozone plays a higher note.
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Explore near-surface ozone by hover, touch or arrow keys: higher ozone plays a higher note, patchy areas sound brighter, east/west pans left/right. Play the timeline to hear it change over two weeks.

modes.name: Precipitation ball
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Place a ball on the moving IMERG precipitation video; rain raises a terrain whose slope rolls the ball around, with Web Audio sound following its motion. Keyboard: focus the map, Enter places the ball, arrows move it. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Scanning line
modes.author: itay
modes.description: A line sweeps across one global IMERG precipitation frame from west to east and plays it as notes on a C major scale, low (C2) at the bottom of the map and high (C5) at the top; the heaviest rain in each band sets that note's volume. From itay's scanning-line-demo branch.

modes.name: Storm watch
modes.summary: Storms in NASA IMERG rain data, tracked over 24 hours. Hover a storm to hear it: north sounds higher, bigger storms louder.
modes.author: itay
modes.description: Follow individual storms through 48 half-hourly IMERG frames, tracked offline with computer vision (OpenCV optical flow and watershed). Hover, or press N and P on the map, to hear about each storm: north sounds higher, bigger storms louder. Enter follows a storm, and when storms merge and split the whole family stays marked; Page Up and Page Down step through time. The full tracking studio with tuning sliders is linked from the panel. From itay's clustering branch.

modes.name: Tone lab
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Hear how each instrument sounds before you hear the data: pick a world instrument from the map or a recorded one, then play a note, a scale, a chord or its typical phrase, from C2 up to A5.

modes.name: Vortex melodies
modes.author: moran
modes.description: Swirling storms in NASA real-time precipitation (IMERG), found by optical flow and tracked over the day. Each swirl loops a short tune: faster spin plays faster, bigger swirls louder; a low hum swells where rain converges.

modes.name: World orchestra
modes.author: moran
modes.description: The world's musical regions on one map. Instruments (on at first): move the mouse, touch, or use the arrow keys, and each region plays a short phrase on a recorded instrument (djembe, kora, oud, balalaika, khomus, morin khuur, sitar, koto, pan flute...). Turn it off and about 280 cities play the data: a city whose value rises past a threshold plays one note in its region's voice.
